description: Controlling and reacting to messages, the Confirm/Enclose failure framework, Failure objects, aborts and interrupts, argument checking, debugging aids (Echo variants, TracePrint, Monitor) and the built-in unit-testing framework (VerificationTest, TestReport).

tools.name: Off
tools.description: Switches off a message so it is not printed: Off[f::tag] for one message, Off[f] for all messages of f, Off[] for all messages, Off[General::stop] to disable the 'further output suppressed' throttle. On reverses it. Use sparingly and prefer Quiet for local suppression.

parameters.name: symbol::tag
parameters.description: Message name, e.g. Power::infy, General::stop.

tools.example:
Off[Solve::ratnz]; sol = Solve[0.5 x^2 == 1, x]; On[Solve::ratnz];
Off[General::stop] (* show every message instead of stopping after 3 *)

tools.name: Quiet
tools.description: Evaluates expr with messages suppressed - all messages, a specific list, or all except a list - without changing the global Off state. It is the safe local way to silence expected warnings such as NIntegrate::ncvb inside a loop.

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression to evaluate (held).

parameters.name: {s::t, ...}
parameters.description: Messages to suppress; All for everything.

parameters.name: third argument
parameters.description: Messages that should still be shown.

tools.example:
Quiet[NIntegrate[Sin[1/x], {x, 0, 1}], NIntegrate::slwcon]
Quiet[Import["missing.csv"]] (* $Failed silently *)
tools.notes: Messages generated inside Quiet are still recorded in $MessageList and are still detectable by Check.

tools.name: Check
tools.description: Evaluates expr and returns failexpr instead if any message (or any of the listed messages) was generated during the evaluation. It is the classic way to turn warnings into control flow, e.g. fall back to a slower method when a fast one complains.
tools.usage:
Check[expr, failexpr]
Check[expr, failexpr, {s1::t1, ...}]
Check[expr, failexpr, "name"]

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression to evaluate.

parameters.name: failexpr
parameters.description: Value returned if a message occurred.

parameters.name: {s::t, ...}
parameters.description: Restrict to specific messages, or a message group name such as "Packing".

tools.example:
res = Check[Quiet[LinearSolve[m, b]], $Failed, LinearSolve::nosol];
Check[NIntegrate[f[x], {x, 0, 1}], NIntegrate[f[x], {x, 0, 1}, MaxRecursion -> 20], NIntegrate::ncvb]
tools.notes: Combine with Quiet to both silence and detect. CheckAbort is the analogue for Abort[].

tools.name: CheckAbort
tools.description: Evaluates expr and, if an Abort[] occurs inside it (or the user interrupts), returns failexpr instead of propagating the abort. Use it to make library code robust against user aborts and to guarantee cleanup such as closing files.

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression that may abort.

parameters.name: failexpr
parameters.description: Value returned on abort.

tools.example: result = CheckAbort[longComputation[], (Close[stream]; $Aborted)]
tools.notes: AbortProtect prevents aborts from taking effect until the block finishes.

tools.name: Abort
tools.description: Abort[] aborts the current evaluation, returning $Aborted, exactly as the user's Alt+. / Evaluation > Abort would. Use it to bail out of deeply nested code where Return or Throw is impractical; Interrupt[] instead opens the interactive interrupt dialog.
tools.example:
If[!FileExistsQ[path], Message[load::nofile, path]; Abort[]]
AbortProtect[WriteString[stream, data]; Close[stream]]
tools.notes: In wolframscript an unhandled Abort ends the script with $Aborted; use Exit[code] for a specific exit status.

tools.name: Assert
tools.description: Assert[test] evaluates test and generates an Assert::asrtf message (and calls $AssertFunction if set) when it is not True. Assertions are ignored unless enabled with On[Assert], making them free in production code.

parameters.name: test
parameters.description: Condition expected to be True.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Optional identifier included in the message.

tools.name: Failure
tools.description: Failure[tag, assoc] is the standard structured failure object returned by many built-ins (Import, URLRead, Interpreter, ResourceFunction) and produced by Confirm/Enclose; assoc typically holds "MessageTemplate", "MessageParameters" and custom data. FailureQ tests for Failure or $Failed. Properties are accessed with f["Message"], f["Tag"], f["Expression"].

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: String or symbol identifying the failure type.

parameters.name: assoc
parameters.description: Association with MessageTemplate, MessageParameters and arbitrary extra keys.

tools.name: Enclose
tools.description: Enclose[expr] evaluates expr and, if any Confirm-family call inside fails, immediately returns the corresponding Failure object instead of continuing; an optional handler function is applied to the failure. It provides structured, exception-like early exit without Throw/Catch tags.
tools.usage:
Enclose[expr]
Enclose[expr, f]
Enclose[expr, f, tag]

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Body containing Confirm/ConfirmBy/ConfirmMatch/ConfirmQuiet/ConfirmAssert calls.

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Handler applied to the Failure object (e.g. Print, or a function returning a default).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Optional tag so nested Enclose blocks catch only their own confirms.

tools.notes: Introduced in 12.2. Enclose is lexically scoped: Confirm calls in functions called from the body are not intercepted unless a tag is passed through.

tools.name: Confirm
tools.description: Confirm[expr] returns expr unless it is a failure ($Failed, Failure[...], $Aborted, Missing[...] etc.), in which case it exits the enclosing Enclose with that failure. ConfirmBy[expr, f] checks a predicate, ConfirmMatch[expr, patt] a pattern, ConfirmAssert[test] a condition and ConfirmQuiet[expr] fails if any message is generated.
tools.usage:
Confirm[expr]
Confirm[expr, info]
ConfirmBy[expr, f]
ConfirmMatch[expr, patt]
ConfirmAssert[test]
ConfirmQuiet[expr]
ConfirmQuiet[expr, {s::t, ...}]

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression to validate; passed through if OK.

parameters.name: info
parameters.description: Optional message or data attached to the generated Failure.

parameters.name: f / patt / test
parameters.description: Predicate, pattern or condition that must succeed.

tools.name: MessageName
tools.description: symbol::tag is the name of a message; assigning a string with backquote slots (`1`, `2`) defines its text, and Message[symbol::tag, args] emits it. Defining messages for your own functions gives users consistent, suppressible diagnostics that integrate with Check, Quiet and Enclose.
tools.usage:
f::tag = "text with `1` and `2`"
Message[f::tag, arg1, arg2]
MessageName[f, "tag"]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Symbol the message belongs to.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Short identifier; General::tag messages are inherited by all symbols.

tools.notes: Messages defined on General (General::argx, General::stop, ...) apply to every symbol.

tools.name: $MessageList
tools.description: List of the message names generated during the current evaluation (as HoldForm[f::tag]); MessageList[n] holds the list for output line n. Use it after Quiet to see what was suppressed or to build custom diagnostics.
tools.example:
Quiet[1/0]; $MessageList (* {HoldForm[Power::infy]} *)
MessageList[%%]

tools.name: $Failed
tools.description: The conventional symbol returned by built-in functions (Get, Import, LibraryFunctionLoad, ToExpression, etc.) when an operation fails. Test for it with === or FailureQ; $Aborted is the analogue returned after Abort[], and $Canceled after a cancelled dialog.
tools.example:
If[(data = Import[file]) === $Failed, Return[$Failed]]
FailureQ[$Failed] (* True *)

tools.name: CheckArguments
tools.description: CheckArguments[f[args], n] or [f[args], {nmin, nmax}] validates the argument count and option names of a call against Options[f], emitting the standard argx/optx messages automatically. Use it in the catch-all definition of a function to get built-in-style error reporting.

parameters.name: f[args]
parameters.description: The actual call expression (held).

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Expected number of positional arguments (or a range).

tools.example:
Options[myFun] = {Tolerance -> 0.01};
myFun[x_, OptionsPattern[]] := x^2
myFun[args___] := Null /; CheckArguments[myFun[args], 1]
myFun[1, 2] (* myFun::argx message *)

tools.name: EchoFunction
tools.description: EchoFunction[f][expr] prints f[expr] (optionally with a label) and returns expr unchanged, letting you inspect intermediate values inside a pipeline without altering results. EchoLabel[label] is the shortcut for a label-only echo, EchoTiming prints the evaluation time and EchoEvaluation shows the unevaluated and evaluated forms.
tools.usage:
EchoFunction[f][expr]
EchoFunction[label, f][expr]
EchoLabel[label][expr]
EchoTiming[expr]
EchoEvaluation[expr]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function applied to expr for display (e.g. Length, Dimensions, Short).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Label printed before the value.

tools.example:
data // EchoFunction["dims", Dimensions] // Transpose // EchoFunction[Length]
EchoTiming[Inverse[RandomReal[1, {500, 500}]]];
tools.notes: Set $EchoFunction to control how all Echo output is rendered (e.g. to log to a file).

tools.name: TracePrint
tools.description: Prints every intermediate expression generated while evaluating expr (indented by depth), optionally only those matching a pattern. Use it as a quick evaluation-order debugger when Trace's nested list is too hard to read.
tools.usage:
TracePrint[expr]
TracePrint[expr, form]
TracePrint[expr, form, opts]

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression to evaluate (held).

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: Pattern restricting what is printed, e.g. _fib or a symbol name.

parameters.name: TraceDepth
parameters.description: Option limiting the nesting depth shown.

tools.example:
fib[n_] := If[n < 2, n, fib[n - 1] + fib[n - 2]]
TracePrint[fib[3], _fib]
tools.notes: TraceScan applies a function to each step; TraceDialog opens an interactive dialog at matching steps.

tools.name: Monitor
tools.description: Monitor[expr, mon] evaluates expr while continuously displaying the current value of mon (typically a loop counter or ProgressIndicator) in a temporary cell that disappears when done. It is the standard progress display for long computations in notebooks.

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Long computation.

parameters.name: mon
parameters.description: Expression re-evaluated dynamically during the computation, e.g. ProgressIndicator[i/n].

tools.example:
Monitor[Do[result[i] = heavy[i], {i, 1, 100}], ProgressIndicator[i, {1, 100}]]
Monitor[NDSolve[eqs, y, {t, 0, 100}, StepMonitor :> (tt = t)], tt]
tools.notes: Only works with a front end; in wolframscript use PrintTemporary or Print. Dynamic updates are throttled to a few per second.

tools.name: PrintTemporary
tools.description: Prints an expression in a temporary cell that is automatically removed when the current evaluation finishes. Use it for status messages that should not clutter the notebook; the returned TemporaryCell object can be deleted early with NotebookDelete.

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression(s) to display temporarily.

tools.name: VerificationTest
tools.description: VerificationTest[input, expected] evaluates input and compares it to expected (with SameTest, default SameQ), also checking expected messages; it returns a TestResultObject with properties like "Outcome", "ActualOutput" and "AbsoluteTimeUsed". Tests are collected in .wlt / .mt files and run with TestReport - the built-in unit-testing framework.
tools.usage:
VerificationTest[input]
VerificationTest[input, expected]
VerificationTest[input, expected, {msg1::tag, ...}]
VerificationTest[input, expected, opts]

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Expression under test (held).

parameters.name: expected
parameters.description: Expected result (default True).

parameters.name: {msgs}
parameters.description: Messages expected during evaluation.

parameters.name: SameTest
parameters.description: Option: comparison function (e.g. Equal, or a tolerance function).

parameters.name: TestID
parameters.description: Option: identifier reported in test results.

parameters.name: TimeConstraint / MemoryConstraint
parameters.description: Options: limits that fail the test when exceeded.

tools.example:
VerificationTest[Prime[5], 11, TestID -> "prime-5"]
VerificationTest[1/0, ComplexInfinity, {Power::infy}]
VerificationTest[N[Pi], 3.14159, SameTest -> (Abs[#1 - #2] < 10^-5 &)]

tools.name: TestReport
tools.description: Runs all VerificationTests in a file, notebook or list and returns a TestReportObject summarizing outcomes, timings and failures with properties such as "TestsSucceededCount", "TestsFailedIndices" and "TestResults". It is the entry point for running test suites headlessly (e.g. from wolframscript in CI).

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Path to a .wlt/.mt test file or a notebook.

parameters.name: HandlerFunctions
parameters.description: Option: callbacks such as "TestEvaluated" for progress reporting.

tools.example:
report = TestReport["tests/core.wlt"];
report["TestsFailedCount"]
report["TestsFailedWrongResults"]
Exit[If[report["AllTestsSucceeded"], 0, 1]]

tools.name: TestResultObject
tools.description: The object returned by VerificationTest, carrying the outcome ("Success", "Failure", "MessagesFailure", "Error"), input, expected and actual output, messages and timing. Query it with obj["prop"] or obj["Properties"]; TestReportObject aggregates many of them.

parameters.name: prop
parameters.description: "Outcome", "Input", "ExpectedOutput", "ActualOutput", "ActualMessages", "AbsoluteTimeUsed", "TestID", ...

tools.name: MissingQ
tools.description: Tests whether an expression is a Missing[...] object, the standard representation of absent data in Dataset, Lookup, EntityValue and Import results. Use it with Select, DeleteMissing and Replace to clean data before numeric processing.

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression to test.

tools.example:
MissingQ[Lookup[<|a -> 1|>, b]] (* True *)
Count[column, _?MissingQ]
column /. _?MissingQ -> 0

tools.name: MessageDialog
tools.description: Opens a modal dialog box displaying an expression with an OK button (or custom buttons). Use it for user-facing errors and notifications in notebook interfaces; in a headless kernel it degrades to a printed message.

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Content to display.

parameters.name: {lbl :> act, ...}
parameters.description: Custom buttons and actions.

parameters.name: WindowTitle
parameters.description: Option: dialog title.

tools.example: MessageDialog["Export finished.", WindowTitle -> "Done"]
tools.notes: ChoiceDialog returns a value from a set of choices; DialogInput builds custom modal dialogs.

tools.name: Beep
tools.description: Beep[] plays the system alert sound, EmitSound plays a Sound or Audio object and Speak reads text aloud through the OS speech engine. Useful as end-of-computation notifications in long notebook sessions.

parameters.name: sound
parameters.description: Sound, Audio or SoundNote expression.

tools.example: NDSolve[bigSystem, ...]; Beep[]; Speak["simulation complete"]

tools.name: TimeRemaining
tools.description: Gives the seconds remaining before the innermost enclosing TimeConstrained limit expires (Infinity if none). Use it inside iterative algorithms to decide whether another iteration fits in the budget and to return a partial result gracefully.
tools.example: TimeConstrained[While[TimeRemaining[] > 0.5, step[]]; best, 10, best]

tools.name: Stack
tools.description: Stack[] gives the list of heads of expressions currently being evaluated (the evaluation stack); Stack[_] gives the full expressions and Stack[patt] those matching a pattern. Use it inside handlers or messages to see where an error came from; StackBegin/StackInhibit control what is recorded.

parameters.name: patt
parameters.description: Pattern restricting which stack entries are returned.

tools.name: Dialog
tools.description: Dialog[] starts an interactive subsession (nested kernel prompt) in which you can inspect and change variables mid-computation; DialogReturn[expr] exits it, returning expr as the value of the Dialog call. Combined with TraceDialog it is the kernel's step-into debugger.
tools.usage:
Dialog[]
Dialog[expr]
DialogReturn[]
DialogReturn[expr]
TraceDialog[expr, form]

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Initial value / expression returned if DialogReturn[] is called without argument.

parameters.name: form
parameters.description: Pattern of intermediate expressions at which TraceDialog pauses.

tools.example:
f[x_] := Module[{y = x^2}, If[y > 100, Dialog[y], y]]
(* in the dialog: y = 50; DialogReturn[y] *)
tools.notes: Only meaningful in interactive sessions; in scripts Dialog returns immediately.

tools.name: Interpretation
tools.description: Interpretation[display, expr] shows display in output but behaves as expr when copied or reused as input. Use it to present rich objects (icons, summaries, formatted results) that remain computable - the mechanism behind summary boxes of ClassifierFunction, Dataset and Failure objects.
tools.usage:
Interpretation[display, expr]
Interpretation[{x = x0, ...}, display, expr]

parameters.name: display
parameters.description: What is shown.

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Underlying value used when the output is evaluated.

tools.example: Interpretation[Style["secret number", Blue], 42] + 1 (* 43 *)

tools.name: General
tools.description: The symbol that holds general messages inherited by all functions: General::argx (wrong argument count), General::stop (further output suppressed), General::ivar, General::spell1, etc. Turning these on/off or redefining their text affects every symbol without its own message of that name.
tools.example:
Off[General::stop] (* never suppress repeated messages *)
Off[General::spell1] (* silence similar-name warnings *)

tools.name: MemoryConstraint
tools.description: Option for VerificationTest (with TimeConstraint) that fails a test if it uses more than the given number of bytes or seconds. Use them to guard against performance regressions in test suites.

parameters.name: TimeConstraint
parameters.description: Seconds allowed (default Infinity).

parameters.name: MemoryConstraint
parameters.description: Bytes allowed (default Infinity).

tools.example: VerificationTest[Sort[RandomReal[1, 10^6]], _List, SameTest -> MatchQ, TimeConstraint -> 2]

tools.name: Once
tools.description: Once[expr] evaluates expr only the first time in a session (or persistently with a location such as "Local"/"KernelSession") and returns the cached value afterwards. It is the simplest memoization for expensive setup such as loading models, compiling code or fetching remote data.

parameters.name: expr
parameters.description: Expression to evaluate once (held).

parameters.name: loc
parameters.description: Persistence location: "KernelSession" (default), "Local", "Cloud", or a PersistenceLocation.

tools.example:
net = Once[NetModel["ResNet-50 Trained on ImageNet Competition Data"]];
data = Once[Import["https://example.com/big.csv"], "Local"];

tools.name: $IterationLimit
tools.description: $IterationLimit (default 4096) bounds the number of successive evaluation steps and $RecursionLimit (default 1024) the depth of nested evaluations; exceeding them produces $IterationLimit::itlim or $RecursionLimit::reclim and a Hold result. Raise them locally with Block for deep recursion.
tools.example:
Block[{$RecursionLimit = 5000}, fib[3000]]
$IterationLimit = Infinity (* risky: infinite loops never stop *)

tools.name: MessagePacket
tools.description: The WSTP/MathLink packet type in which the kernel sends messages to a front end or client program; along with TextPacket, ReturnPacket and ReturnExpressionPacket it is what a custom link reader (LinkRead) receives. Relevant when driving a kernel from C, Java, .NET or Python via raw links.

tools.name: Interrupt
tools.description: Interrupt[] programmatically triggers the same interrupt as the user's Alt+. / Evaluation > Interrupt, opening the interrupt dialog in a notebook (abort, continue, enter subsession) or aborting in a headless kernel. Useful for debugging checkpoints in long computations.
tools.example: If[Abs[residual] > 10^6, Interrupt[]]

tools.name: $AssertFunction
tools.description: Function applied to a failed Assert (after assertions are enabled with On[Assert]); it receives the held assertion expression. Set it to Throw or a custom logger to convert assertion failures into exceptions or reports.
